html:
The Dharug, or Darug, are a nation of Aboriginal Australian clans whose Country covers much of the region of present-day Sydney. The clans share ties of kinship, country and culture, and spoke coastal and inland dialects of the Dharug language. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

They lived as hunters, fishers and gatherers across the Cumberland Plain, along the Hawkesbury and Nepean rivers, and around the harbour. When the First Fleet arrived in 1788, Dharug-speaking clans were among the first people to meet the British. In 1789 smallpox killed a great many of them.

As farms spread along the rivers, the Dharug fought back in the Hawkesbury and Nepean Wars from 1795 to 1816. The resistance leader Pemulwuy led raids around Parramatta until he was shot in 1802. Neighbours included the Tharawal to the south, the Gundungurra to the southwest and the Darkinyung to the north. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
